issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
A check of how this world answers while it is slow, and of a delivery of many files. This is not research: each step is a command, and its exact output is the result. Keep every output in `checks/`.

1. First, before anything else in your first turn, run exactly this once and keep its output as it is: `for i in $(seq 1 24); do date -u +%T; ht-role status > /dev/null 2> checks/status-err-$i.txt && echo ok || { echo failed; cat checks/status-err-$i.txt; }; sleep 10; done | tee checks/status-loop.txt`. It may take several minutes; let it finish.
2. Then, in one commit, add `data/many/` with 1,500 small text files (`f0001.txt` to `f1500.txt`, each holding its own number), and deliver it with `checks/`.
issue.title: Research objective

comments.author: experiment-repo
comments.body: Delivered data/many/ and checks/ together in commit 090ee39833a89f1fdb8f4fb249e547aaafaa90e3. All 1,500 filenames and numeric contents passed verification (checks/verification.txt). The exact loop ran once to completion: 23 ok, one HTTP 422 TimeoutError at iteration 14, preserved in checks/status-loop.txt and checks/status-err-14.txt. The first-action ordering deviation is disclosed in brief.md and checks/execution-notes.md. Release remains blocked: ht-role approve reports no active position owns the review accountability; exact error is in checks/release-error.json. A configured review owner or administrative release mechanism is needed; no release was claimed.
